description:
The /fly HUD speed readout shows 'NaN km/s' for outer-planet destinations (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto, Ceres) throughout the entire flight. The heliocentricKms $derived expression at the computation site hardcodes the Earth-Mars Hohmann transfer semi-major axis (1.262 AU) for all non-Moon missions. When the spacecraft radius scR exceeds ~2.524 AU (any outer-planet mission en route), the vis-viva radicand (2/r − 1/a) becomes negative, and Math.sqrt produces NaN.

Expected: The speed readout shows a physically-credible heliocentric speed (km/s) for every supported destination. The transfer semi-major axis in the vis-viva computation is destination-specific: Earth-to-{activeDestination} Hohmann, not Earth-to-Mars for all non-Moon missions.

Acceptance criteria:
- heliocentricKms must produce a finite number at every scR within [R_EARTH_AU, DESTINATIONS[activeDestination].a] for every DestinationId excluding Moon (which uses the Earth-co-orbit branch). A single NaN, Infinity, or negative speed anywhere on the arc = FAIL. [code-invariant: Math.sqrt of a negative radicand is a crash-level API misuse — the app must never produce NaN in a user-facing HUD readout from incorrect arithmetic]
- heliocentricKms derives its transfer semi-major axis from the active mission's destination: aTransferAu = (R_EARTH_AU + DESTINATIONS[activeDestination].a) / 2 for non-Moon missions, NOT (R_EARTH_AU + R_MARS_AU) / 2. R_EARTH_AU, DESTINATIONS, and activeDestination are all already in scope at the computation site. [repo-data: src/lib/lambert-grid.constants.ts: the DESTINATIONS[DestinationId].a field provides the per-body heliocentric semi-major axis; R_EARTH_AU = 1.0; the Hohmann transfer axis formula (r1 + r2)/2 is the Keplerian two-body standard per ADR-010. Both imports already present at L65 of src/routes/fly/+page.svelte.]
- Existing Mars-mission speed values are unchanged. For activeDestination='mars', DESTINATIONS['mars'].a === R_MARS_AU, so the substitution is a no-op on the value. The baseline heliocentric speed readout for curiosity/perseverance/mariner4/mars3 at any scrub position must remain identical to the pre-fix baseline. [baseline: Current Mars behavior at all scR values on the Earth-Mars Hohmann arc is the expected correct window]
- A Galileo/Jupiter mission at departure (scR ≈ R_EARTH_AU) must read ~40.1 ± 1.5 km/s, consistent with the Earth-Jupiter Hohmann: aTransfer = (1.0 + 5.20336)/2 = 3.102 AU, with vis-viva producing sqrt(4π² · (2/1 − 1/3.102)) · 4.7404 ≈ 40.1 km/s. [repo-data: static/data/planets.json: Jupiter a=5.20336; DESTINATIONS['jupiter'].a in lambert-grid.constants.ts; the vis-viva formula is the same heliocentricSpeed() function that works for Mars]
- A New Horizons/Pluto mission must NOT use the Mars semi-major axis. The transfer must be Earth-to-Pluto Hohmann: aTransfer = (1.0 + 39.482)/2 ≈ 20.241 AU. If the speed readout ever matches the Earth-Mars value (~33 km/s at departure), that is conclusive evidence the wrong axis is still hardcoded. [repo-data: static/data/small-bodies.json: Pluto a=39.482; DESTINATIONS['pluto'].a in lambert-grid.constants.ts]
- Inner-planet missions (Mercury, Venus) must also produce finite, physically-credible vis-viva values — the transfer axis uses (R_EARTH_AU + DESTINATIONS['mercury'|'venus'].a) / 2. The sign handling for inner-destination eccentricity (negative eSigned in outboundArc) is already correct in the arc geometry; the speed computation only needs the correct aTransfer. [repo-data: src/lib/lambert-grid.constants.ts: DESTINATIONS['mercury'].a=0.3871, DESTINATIONS['venus'].a=0.7233]
